title: The Quiet Connection
caseDescription: A string of disappearances has one faint connection: each victim used the same dating platform. Somewhere among these ten profiles, a pattern is waiting to be noticed.

title: The Midnight Check-In
caseDescription: Three travelers vanished after arranging private city meetups. Their last known locations form a trail through the same late-night check-in network. One of these ten profiles is hiding how well he knows the route.

title: The Vanishing Hours
caseDescription: Several women disappeared after meeting people through the same dating network. Each case includes a gap in the evening timeline, and one of these ten profiles knows exactly how to make those hours disappear.

title: The Borrowed Alibi
caseDescription: A chain of disappearances points to borrowed names, copied routines, and alibis that sound almost too polished. Among these ten profiles, one person has been hiding behind someone else’s story.

title: The Blue Hour Signal
caseDescription: Three women vanished during the blue hour between sunset and nightfall. Their phones went quiet near the same riverside signal tower, and one profile knows why the tower mattered.

title: The House with No Address
caseDescription: Each missing person received an invitation to a house that did not appear on any map. The invitations looked personal, but their wording reveals one careful author hiding among these profiles.

title: The Borrowed Voice
caseDescription: The victims all heard the same comforting voice before they disappeared, though the calls came from different numbers. One profile has been collecting other people’s phrases a little too carefully.

title: The Last Ferry Home
caseDescription: Three people boarded the last ferry across the lake and never reached the other side. The timetable appears ordinary until travel records, weather, and private messages are compared.

title: The Orchard of Alibis
caseDescription: A rural orchard becomes the common thread in disappearances that were reported miles apart. Everyone has a reason to have been nearby, but one alibi repeats details from another person’s account.

title: The Unsent Invitations
caseDescription: Several victims received invitations that vanished from their inboxes before anyone could open them. The sender kept no visible account, yet one profile’s activity mirrors every missing invitation.

title: The Glass Thread
caseDescription: Tiny fragments of blue glass connect four disappearance sites, but the material is common enough to mislead. The decisive clue is a thread linking the victims to a place one profile denies visiting.

title: The Witness in Every Photo
caseDescription: Every disappearance has a photograph taken nearby, and the same unseen witness appears in the reflections. The final case rewards patient comparison: the truth is hidden in what each image leaves out.

title: The Last Seen Playlist
caseDescription: Three people vanished after sharing the same late-night playlist. The songs are harmless on their own, but one profile keeps appearing in the listening history just before each disappearance.

title: The Empty Platform
caseDescription: A commuter disappears from a station platform with no usable camera footage. Ten profiles share the same transit app, but only one has been quietly changing the records after midnight.

title: The Glasshouse Alibi
caseDescription: A private greenhouse becomes the last known location in a string of disappearances. The killer has built an alibi from weather reports, delivery logs, and one carefully planted photograph.

title: The Borrowed Weekend
caseDescription: Several dates end with a weekend trip that nobody remembers agreeing to. One profile has been borrowing other people’s plans, locations, and excuses to make every meeting look accidental.

title: The Silent Checkpoint
caseDescription: A string of disappearances follows a route through quiet border towns. Messages were deleted, checkpoints were skipped, and one profile knows the route without ever admitting to taking it.

title: The False Emergency
caseDescription: Victims received urgent messages from people they trusted, then disappeared while trying to help. The emergency was always convincing, and one profile understands exactly how to manufacture panic.

title: The Night Archive
caseDescription: Old case files reveal a pattern that the current disappearances repeat almost perfectly. Someone has been studying the archive closely enough to turn forgotten mistakes into a new method.

title: The Perfect Witness
caseDescription: Every disappearance has a witness, every witness has a story, and every story points somewhere else. The final case is built on a perfect account that may have been rehearsed from the beginning.
